Task: Determine workflow for Taxonomies dropdown in design
Github Title: Define workflow for Taxonomies dropdown in Studio design
Github Description:
## Use Case

As a Platform Administrator, I need a clear and intuitive way to navigate to and manage Competency Taxonomies and tag taxonomies from the Studio home page so that I can quickly access the taxonomies I care about without confusion about what each option does.

---

## Description

The UX Designer has proposed a dropdown on the Taxonomies tab of the Studio home page with two options: "Competency" and "Tags". In the current design, clicking either option launches the taxonomy import wizard with the corresponding Taxonomy Type pre-selected.

Two concerns have been raised with this design:

1. **Labeling:** Nothing in the current design indicates that clicking an option starts an import/creation flow. A user clicking "Competency" will likely expect to see their competency taxonomies — not be taken into an import wizard. This is a significant discoverability risk.  
     
2. **Use case frequency:** Platform Administrators will far more often want to view and manage existing taxonomies than to create new ones from the home page. The import wizard is already accessible via the Import button on the Taxonomies page itself.

Three directions are on the table for the designer to evaluate:

**Option A — Navigation only:** Dropdown options navigate to the Taxonomies page pre-filtered by type ("Competency Taxonomies", "Tag Taxonomies"). Import stays on the Taxonomies page as it currently is. Note: this requires filter/tab functionality on the Taxonomies page, which would expand the scope of ticket 7\.

**Option B — Navigation \+ creation:** Four options — "View Competency Taxonomies", "View Tag Taxonomies", "Add Competency Taxonomy", "Add Tag Taxonomy". Covers both the management and creation use cases, at the cost of a more complex dropdown.

**Option C — Label fix only:** Retain the current import-only behavior but update the labels to make the action unambiguous — for example, "Add Competency Taxonomy" and "Add Tag Taxonomy", or prefix each with "+". Lowest-effort change; does not address the frequency-of-use concern.

The designer should evaluate these options (and any alternatives) and produce a revised design. The chosen direction feeds directly into ticket 7\.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

This is a design spike. The deliverable is design artifacts and documented decisions, not working code. There is no Gherkin and no QA path.

- [ ] The three options above (and any designer alternatives) have been reviewed with the team and a direction has been chosen with documented rationale  
- [ ] The revised design clearly communicates to the user what action each dropdown option performs before they click it  
- [ ] Figma or design file is updated to reflect the agreed-upon approach  
- [ ] If Option A or B is chosen, the design specifies how filtering behaves on the Taxonomies page and notes are added to ticket 7 to expand its scope accordingly  
- [ ] Notes for ticket 7 are written capturing the agreed workflow, interaction details, and any new filtering or navigation requirements the implementation will need

---

## Context for the Designer

**Current import workflow** (from ticket 4 — what the existing design routes users into):

1. Click Import on the Taxonomies page  
2. Upload a JSON or CSV file  
3. Click Continue  
4. Fill in Taxonomy Name, Taxonomy Description, and Taxonomy Type (dropdown: Tags default, Competency option)  
5. Click Import

**Taxonomy types available to users:** "Competency" and "Tags" only. System-level taxonomies exist but cannot be user-created and should not appear as dropdown options.

**Filtering capability:** The Taxonomies page does not currently have filter or tab functionality. If Option A or B is chosen, this will need to be built as part of ticket 7 — budget accordingly.

**Related tickets:**

- Ticket 4: Import flow with Taxonomy Type dropdown (the flow the current design leads into)  
- Ticket 5: Taxonomy type badge on taxonomy cards (the visual that makes filtering meaningful)  
- Ticket 7: Implementation of whichever design this ticket produces  
- \[Link to current Figma design\]
Questions: Ready for community review (pending comment from Phil in ticket). Does Jenna want to move forward with Option B or Option D (remove from scope). If Option D, do we also want to remove filtering taxonomies by Competency vs Tags from scope as well?

Github Title: Implement Competency Criteria data model described in ADR 0023 and ADR 0024
Github Description:
Use Case:
As a Platform Administrator, I need to configure Competency Criteria associations for courses.

Description:
Implement the Competency Criteria data model described in ADR 0023 and ADR 0024 to support authoring, storing, retrieving, evaluating, and auditing competency achievement criteria in Open edX.

The implementation should include the core authoring models needed to represent a full Competency Achievement Criteria expression tree:

- CompetencyTaxonomy, using Django multi-table inheritance from Taxonomy, to identify taxonomies that are enabled for competency-related workflows.
- CompetencyCriteriaGroup, representing internal nodes in a competency criteria tree. Groups should support parent-child relationships, competency tag association, optional course scope, name, ordering, and AND / OR logic.
- CompetencyCriteria, representing leaf criteria in the tree. Each criterion should belong to a CompetencyCriteriaGroup, reference an oel_tagging_objecttag association, optionally reference a CompetencyRuleProfile, and support rule type and payload overrides.
- CompetencyRuleProfile, representing reusable default evaluation rules scoped to organization, course, and/or competency taxonomy.

The implementation should also include the learner status models needed to materialize and preserve competency evaluation results:

- CompetencyMasteryStatuses, seeded with the supported mastery status values.
- StudentCompetencyCriteriaStatus, storing learner status at the individual criterion level.
- StudentCompetencyCriteriaGroupStatus, storing learner status at the criteria group level.
- StudentCompetencyStatus, storing learner status at the overall competency level.

The data model should support nested criteria trees, deterministic evaluation ordering, course-scoped criteria, default and override rule behavior, and efficient lookup patterns through the indexes described in the ADRs.

The implementation should also follow the lifecycle and traceability decisions from ADR 0024:

- Apply django-simple-history to CompetencyCriteriaGroup, CompetencyCriteria, and CompetencyRuleProfile.
- Do not apply django-simple-history to oel_tagging_tag, oel_tagging_taxonomy, or CompetencyTaxonomy in this phase.
- Treat learner status models as append-only history.
- Protect or archive competency definition records after related learner status exists, according to the ADR-defined delete and archive rules.

Github Title: Build asynchronous listener to evaluate learner competency statuses from grade persistence events
Github Description:
Use Case:
As a Learner, when an assignment or course associated to Competency Criteria is completed, the learner’s competency mastery status should be evaluated and saved to the platform.

Description:
Build a listener that responds to grade persistence events for assignments, courses, or other supported graded objects that may be associated with Competency Criteria.

When a grade is persisted for an object associated with Competency Criteria, the system should retrieve the relevant criteria, asynchronously evaluate the learner’s status, update criterion-level status, recompute group-level status, and update the overall competency status.

The listener should support the mastery rules defined by the relevant Competency Criteria and Competency Rule Profile behavior.

Acceptance Criteria:
Given an assignment is associated with Competency Criteria
And a learner completes the assignment
When the completion event is processed
Then the learner's competency mastery status is evaluated
And the updated status is saved to the platform

Given a course is associated with Competency Criteria
And a learner completes the course
When the completion event is processed
Then the learner's competency mastery status is evaluated
And the updated status is saved to the platform

Given an assignment or course is not associated with Competency Criteria
When the learner completes the assignment or course
Then no competency mastery status calculation is triggered

Given Competency Criteria and applicable rule profile data exist
When the learner's competency mastery status is evaluated
Then the calculation uses the relevant criteria and rule profile values
And the saved status reflects the calculation result

Given a learner's competency mastery status is updated
When the updated status is saved
Then the platform stores the status according to the defined data model
And the update can be retrieved for learner progress workflows

Given a grade persists for content associated with Competency Criteria
When the asynchronous evaluation process handles the event
Then the relevant Competency Criteria are retrieved
And the learner's criterion, criteria group, and competency statuses are evaluated and saved
